why: tripwire: High-yield credit spread is newly unusual (z +1.3 -> +2.0)
key_risks: Binary: FOMC on Dec 8-9 (NOTE:A1). A hike toward the SEP 4.1% into widening credit could tip HY spreads past 4.5. Pullback risk (0.149) may understate this because the model omits HY spreads.
Binary: OPEC+ meeting on Nov 29 on 2027 quotas (NOTE:E12). A supply increase versus a cut moves oil and energy sharply.
Binary: further Iranian mine attacks in Hormuz or Gulf refinery strikes (NOTE:E7, NOTE:E16) could spike oil despite the IEA surplus.

Consumer sentiment (UMCSENT 48, record 5yr low) directly contradicts strong hard data (retail sales +6.82% YoY, strong Discretionary momentum); a reconciliation either way (soft data catching down hard data, or vice versa) is a swing risk for Consumer Discretionary.
Dec 4 Employment Situation (binary for labor market)

December 8-9 FOMC/SEP is a binary rate-path risk: inflation is running well above the Fed's 2026 target dot (PCEPILFE 3.26% vs SEP_JCXFEMD_2026 3.4% median, but CPI 4.08% is hotter), raising the chance the SEP shifts hawkish versus market pricing of further hikes already embedded in the 2yr yield.
FOMC Dec 8-9 with SEP (binary for rates path)
FOMC December 8-9 meeting (NOTE:A1) could deliver a hawkish Summary of Economic Projections given CPI at 4.08% (FRED:CPIAUCSL: 4.08) and 2-year yield at 4.61% (FRED:DGS2: 4.61).

HY credit spread tripwire (BAMLH0A0HYM2 z +1.3 -> +2.0, 96th percentile, widening fast) is a genuine new stress signal that CALC:recession_risk and CALC:pullback_risk underweight directly (they use NFCI/yield-curve/realized-vol, not HY spread level as a top driver), so an acceleration here could invalidate the 'normal' reading from both models.

High-yield credit spread widening (FRED:BAMLH0A0HYM2: 3.77) crosses into acute stress (z=+2.01), which could cascade into broader equity market liquidations given S&P 500 is already below its 200-day average (-0.8%, CALC:risk_indicators).

Hormuz mine strikes (Nov 26, at least 2 ships hit) and Houthi attack on Saudi's largest refinery (Nov 25) are fresh escalations on top of an already-closed Strait since Feb 2026; a confirmed loss of physical tanker throughput (vs. threats already priced) would be a binary oil-upside shock beyond the factor forecast.
OPEC+ 21-country meeting on November 29, 2026 (NOTE:E12) deciding 2027 production quotas amid Strait of Hormuz mine attacks (NOTE:E7) could trigger sharp binary moves in oil prices.

OPEC+ full 21-country meeting on Nov 29 to set 2027 quotas is a binary near-term event that could push oil sharply either way depending on whether it signals discipline or a supply response to the IEA-reported surplus.
Pullback risk model p_10pct_3m is 0.149 (CALC:pullback_risk), but realized volatility is at the 96th percentile (32%) and VIX is 26.8 (FRED:VIXCLS: 26.8), indicating heightened tail-risk.
Russia-NATO spillover: missiles in Poland (NOTE:E4) and Estonia's border closure on Dec 1 (NOTE:E17).
The CPI release on Dec 10 could show headline CPI above 4%, reinforcing hike pricing.
